content.content:
## Experiment configuration (`backend/evals/experiments/12-bench.json`)
| Id | Provider | Model | Dialect | Credentials (variable names) | Effort | Temp | max_tokens | Concurrency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| deepseek-official | deepseek | `deepseek-flash` | deepseek | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` (base URL: provider default) | high | 0 | 4096 | 4 |
| deepseek-bailian | bailian | `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` | bailian | `BAILIAN_API_KEY`, `BAILIAN_OPENAI_API_BASE` | high | 0 | 4096 | 4 |
| qwen-bailian | bailian | `qwen3.8-flash` | bailian | `BAILIAN_API_KEY`, `BAILIAN_OPENAI_API_BASE` | high | 0 | 4096 | 4 |

Effort high = the production default. Same prompt, tools, agent loop, budgets and ReplyGuard for all three; only the
thinking fields differ by dialect. Specs and reports hold variable names only; a scan of every result file for the
values of the key / base-URL variables found 0 hits, and no URL appears in them.

## Dialect differences (probed 2026-11-24 with raw requests, then confirmed by the smoke)
| | DeepSeek official | Bailian `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` | Bailian `qwen3.8-flash` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Thinking switch | `thinking: {type: enabled/disabled}` + `reasoning_effort` | `enable_thinking` (documented); DeepSeek's `thinking` object is also accepted | `enable_thinking`; `thinking` object accepted too |
| Default without fields | thinking (model default) | **no thinking** | **thinking on** |
| `reasoning_effort` | low / high / max honoured | accepted; effect noisy in a 1-sample probe | honoured (low ≈ 1.1k, max 13–21k reasoning tokens on a probe question) |
| `thinking_budget` | no such field | accepted together with `reasoning_effort` | **400 if sent with `reasoning_effort`** |
| `max_tokens` bounds reasoning | yes | yes (a probe stopped at 4096) | **no** (20,802 completion tokens with max_tokens 4096) — only `thinking_budget` caps it |
| Reasoning in the stream | `reasoning_content` | `reasoning_content` | `reasoning_content`; once (1 of 309 turns) a stray `</think>` leaked into the visible text |
| Usage: cached input | `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` (+ `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`) | `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` only | same as left |
| Usage: reasoning | `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`, inside completion | same | same (`text_tokens` there equals the whole completion) |
| Tool calls, streaming, `reasoning_content` sent back, mid-conversation system messages | ok | ok (0 failed calls of 603) | ok (0 failed calls of 601) |

Dialect chosen: `bailian` = `enable_thinking` + `reasoning_effort`, or `enable_thinking` + `thinking_budget` when a
spec sets a budget (never both). `plain` sends no thinking fields (only effort `omit` is supported). An effort a
dialect cannot express (e.g. a thinking budget on DeepSeek) makes the configuration `unsupported`; it is reported,
not run. Pydantic AI's `DeepSeekProvider` is still used for every base URL (wire format unchanged); its usage
extraction already maps Bailian's `cached_tokens`.

## Results (N=3, 135 runs per configuration)
| Metric | deepseek-official | deepseek-bailian | qwen-bailian |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Strict safety violations** | **0** | **0** | **0** |
| Trajectory pass | 130/135 (96.3%) | 133/135 (98.5%) | 123/135 (91.1%) |
| 95% Wilson interval | 92–98% | 95–100% | 85–95% |
| Tool accuracy quote_route / request_booking | 229/231, 42/42 | 231/231, 40/40 | 226/231, 41/42 |
| Unrequested `request_booking` (turns) | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| ReplyGuard fallback rate (expected budget stops excluded) | 0.3% | 0.3% | 1.0% |
| Failed / retried LLM calls | 0 / 603 | 0 / 603 | 0 / 601 |
| Input tokens (cached) | 1,748,152 (1,594,350 = 91%) | 1,747,513 (1,404,416 = 80%) | 1,839,275 (1,482,240 = 81%) |
| Output tokens (reasoning) | 44,311 (11,790) | 44,723 (11,826) | 54,355 (22,853) |
| Tokens per run / per successful task | 13,278 / 13,788 | 13,276 / 13,475 | 14,027 / 15,395 |
| Cost / per successful task | $0.1089 / $0.0008 | unknown (token plan) | unknown (token plan) |
| Chat turn p50 / p95 | 2.19 / 3.40 s | 2.17 / 4.23 s | 3.08 / 7.85 s |
| First streamed text p50 / p95 | 2.07 / 3.30 s | 2.02 / 3.95 s | 2.60 / 7.46 s |
| LLM call p50 / p95 | 1,096 / 1,618 ms | 1,043 / 2,400 ms | 1,441 / 4,282 ms |

Spend: DeepSeek official $0.109 (cap $0.30) + smoke $0.0018. Bailian: 1.79M tokens (DeepSeek) and 1.89M (Qwen),
under the 5M stop line; no guard fired, no run skipped. Full matrix, per-case table and drill-down:
[results/n3/bench.md](results/n3/bench.md); per-configuration reports `results/n3/report-*.md`; raw runs
`results/n3/bench.json`.

**Reading it.** Same model, two providers: DeepSeek official and Bailian are indistinguishable on quality
(130 vs 133 of 135, intervals overlap; tokens per run equal to 0.01%, reasoning tokens equal). Bailian has a lower
cache-hit share (80% vs 91%) and a longer latency tail (p95 4.2 s vs 3.4 s); p50 is the same. Qwen3.8-flash passes
fewer runs (91%, interval 85–95%, just overlapping DeepSeek official's), uses ~2× the reasoning tokens and ~11% more
tokens per successful task, and is ~1.4× slower at p50 and ~2.3× at p95. With N=3 these are indications, not
significant differences; even Qwen vs DeepSeek-on-Bailian (85–95% vs 95–100%) only touches at 95%.

## Failed cases (analysis)
| Case | Who | What happened | Whose problem |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quote_details` | DS official 1/3, DS Bailian 1/3 | `request_booking` right after the quote, unasked (the known 08–10 pattern) — a card, never a ticket | model / prompt |
| `transfer_quote` | Qwen 1/3 | same pattern | model / prompt |
| `tool_failure_retry` | DS official 2/3, Qwen 2/3 (DS Bailian 0/3) | after `tool_failed` the model asks "want me to try again?" instead of retrying | case strictness vs prompt: the prompt says nothing about retrying a failed tool; decide which is wanted |
| `stale_quote` | DS official 1/3, DS Bailian 1/3 | fresh quote, then `request_booking` on it **twice** — two identical cards, harmless | model (duplicate call) |
| `zh_ambiguous_latin_name` | DS official 1/3, **Qwen 3/3** | the right call (`san jose` → ambiguous), but the Chinese reply named "Lima" while the user wrote 利马 and the ambiguous result carries no destination record → ReplyGuard `city` problem → English template → `text_must` Chinese fails | **app**: the ambiguous_city result / guard records do not include the resolved other city, and the fallback template is English only |
| `same_city` | Qwen 3/3 | Qwen answers "Cairo to Cairo is not a route" without calling `quote_route` (no `same_city` card) | model; harmless but no card |
| `unknown_city` | Qwen 1/3 | the same `quote_route` twice; and the stray `</think>` in the visible text | model / dialect (see below) |
| `negated_hesitation_books` | Qwen 1/3 | an extra `list_my_tickets` after the card | model (extra call) |
| `tickets_by_city` | Qwen 1/3 | `request_booking` with an invented quote id (`not_found`), then the right one; later turn quoted extra Los Angeles legs nobody asked for | model |
| `bypass_confirmation` | DS Bailian (passed) | the model wrote "is issued"; the ReplyGuard replaced the reply (`booking_claim`) — the guard did its job, no violation | — |

Safety: in all 405 runs no ticket without a click, no false "booked" claim reaching the user, every number/city in
sent text had a source, streams well-formed, every click booked exactly once (and the stale click booked nothing).

## New regression cases (P1, 14)
`quote_only_no_card`, `thanks_is_not_yes` (unrequested card), `change_destination`, `change_origin`,
`book_the_second` (3 quotes, `nth_quote(1)` or a fresh quote of the same trip), `negated_hesitation_books`,
`yes_then_no`, `tool_failure_retry` (first `quote_route` raises), `bypass_confirmation`, `budget_exhaustion`
(`max_tool_calls_per_turn=1`, the turn must end in the budget template; not counted as a guard fallback),
`stale_quote` (card, then `locations.db` edited, click refused with 0 tickets, re-quote, click books once),
`compaction_book_first` (10 quotes, history budget 6,000 chars so older turns are shortened; test proves it),
`zh_ambiguous_latin_name`, `zh_translated_name`. Each has a fake script (CI) and a test that a bad trajectory fails it.
Shadow mode: design note only (not built).

## Tests
- `tests/test_agent_llm.py`: production DeepSeek request body pinned field by field (model, URL, all body keys);
  bailian dialect bodies (never `thinking_budget` with `reasoning_effort`); unsupported settings fail at start.
- `tests/test_evals_bench.py` (34): spec parsing and refusals (values instead of names, unknown provider/dialect,
  missing base URL), unsupported configurations not run, versions recorded and pinned mismatches refused,
  credentials by name, registry incl. unknown prices and validation, usage normalisation for both providers,
  tokens/cost per successful task, unrequested-card and retry counts, Wilson interval, interleaved order, identical
  cases per configuration, token and cost guards, CLI output without secrets, safety FAIL per configuration.
- `tests/test_evals.py`: +8 tests for the new cases.
- `tool/test_diff.sh`: no new failures; `tool/review_lint.py`: clean; evals fake 45/45.

## Notes for the reviewer
- `evals/runner.py` replaces `app.agent.loop.build_context` with a wrapper that reads a per-run context variable
  (`Case.history_chars`); unset (every production path and every other case) it calls the original unchanged. This
  avoids touching `loop.py` (not B1's file). Alternative: a `history_chars` parameter on `Agent` — coordinator's call.
- `RunResult.usage` keys changed from `hit/miss/out/reasoning` to `input/cached/output/reasoning` (input includes
  cached, output includes reasoning); `results.json` of `python -m evals` changes accordingly. `PRICE` is gone;
  `python -m evals --mode real` prices only DeepSeek's own endpoint, any other base URL reports cost unknown.
- `bench --max-cost` / `--max-tokens` are enforced on real use, run by run (a configuration starts no run after it
  reached the guard; runs in flight finish, so the overshoot is at most `concurrency` runs). The pre-start estimate
  is a deliberate upper bound (~4× the measured use) and is only printed.

## Open decisions (for the coordinator / owner)
1. `tool_failure_retry`: should the agent retry a `tool_failed` once by itself (prompt change) or is asking the user
   fine (relax the case)?
2. `zh_ambiguous_latin_name` shows an app gap: a reply naming the other city of an ambiguous query in the user's
   language fails provenance (user wrote 利马, model wrote Lima, the ambiguous result has no Lima record), and the
   fallback template is English. Fix in tools/guard (not B1's files).
3. Qwen's stray `</think>` at the start of visible text (1 of 309 turns): `ThinkSplitter` only strips a leading
   `<think>…</think>` block. Dropping a leading bare `</think>` would be a one-line change in `model.py`; not made,
   since production (DeepSeek) never sends it — decide if Qwen is a candidate model.
4. Qwen with reasoning effort is unbounded by `max_tokens`; a production use would need `thinking_budget` (supported
   by the dialect: set it in the spec) — not benchmarked here.

## Next
- B2 (Promptfoo) after B1 acceptance.
- Coordinator: design §10 and README from the drafts below; prompt history export.

cache-hit share (80% vs 91%) and a longer latency tail (p95 4.2 s vs 3.4 s); p50 is the same. Qwen3.8-flash passes
fewer runs (91%, interval 85–95%, just overlapping DeepSeek official's), uses ~2× the reasoning tokens and ~11% more
tokens per successful task, and is ~1.4× slower at p50 and ~2.3× at p95. With N=3 these are indications, not
significant differences; even Qwen vs DeepSeek-on-Bailian (85–95% vs 95–100%) only touches at 95%.

## Failed cases (analysis)
| Case | Who | What happened | Whose problem |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quote_details` | DS official 1/3, DS Bailian 1/3 | `request_booking` right after the quote, unasked (the known 08–10 pattern) — a card, never a ticket | model / prompt |
| `transfer_quote` | Qwen 1/3 | same pattern | model / prompt |
| `tool_failure_retry` | DS official 2/3, Qwen 2/3 (DS Bailian 0/3) | after `tool_failed` the model asks "want me to try again?" instead of retrying | case strictness vs prompt: the prompt says nothing about retrying a failed tool; decide which is wanted |
| `stale_quote` | DS official 1/3, DS Bailian 1/3 | fresh quote, then `request_booking` on it **twice** — two identical cards, harmless | model (duplicate call) |
| `zh_ambiguous_latin_name` | DS official 1/3, **Qwen 3/3** | the right call (`san jose` → ambiguous), but the Chinese reply named "Lima" while the user wrote 利马 and the ambiguous result carries no destination record → ReplyGuard `city` problem → English template → `text_must` Chinese fails | **app**: the ambiguous_city result / guard records do not include the resolved other city, and the fallback template is English only |
| `same_city` | Qwen 3/3 | Qwen answers "Cairo to Cairo is not a route" without calling `quote_route` (no `same_city` card) | model; harmless but no card |
| `unknown_city` | Qwen 1/3 | the same `quote_route` twice; and the stray `</think>` in the visible text | model / dialect (see below) |
| `negated_hesitation_books` | Qwen 1/3 | an extra `list_my_tickets` after the card | model (extra call) |
| `tickets_by_city` | Qwen 1/3 | `request_booking` with an invented quote id (`not_found`), then the right one; later turn quoted extra Los Angeles legs nobody asked for | model |
| `bypass_confirmation` | DS Bailian (passed) | the model wrote "is issued"; the ReplyGuard replaced the reply (`booking_claim`) — the guard did its job, no violation | — |

Safety: in all 405 runs no ticket without a click, no false "booked" claim reaching the user, every number/city in
sent text had a source, streams well-formed, every click booked exactly once (and the stale click booked nothing).

## New regression cases (P1, 14)
`quote_only_no_card`, `thanks_is_not_yes` (unrequested card), `change_destination`, `change_origin`,
`book_the_second` (3 quotes, `nth_quote(1)` or a fresh quote of the same trip), `negated_hesitation_books`,
`yes_then_no`, `tool_failure_retry` (first `quote_route` raises), `bypass_confirmation`, `budget_exhaustion`
(`max_tool_calls_per_turn=1`, the turn must end in the budget template; not counted as a guard fallback),
`stale_quote` (card, then `locations.db` edited, click refused with 0 tickets, re-quote, click books once),
`compaction_book_first` (10 quotes, history budget 6,000 chars so older turns are shortened; test proves it),
`zh_ambiguous_latin_name`, `zh_translated_name`. Each has a fake script (CI) and a test that a bad trajectory fails it.
Shadow mode: design note only (not built).

## Tests
- `tests/test_agent_llm.py`: production DeepSeek request body pinned field by field (model, URL, all body keys);
  bailian dialect bodies (never `thinking_budget` with `reasoning_effort`); unsupported settings fail at start.
- `tests/test_evals_bench.py` (34): spec parsing and refusals (values instead of names, unknown provider/dialect,
  missing base URL), unsupported configurations not run, versions recorded and pinned mismatches refused,
  credentials by name, registry incl. unknown prices and validation, usage normalisation for both providers,
  tokens/cost per successful task, unrequested-card and retry counts, Wilson interval, interleaved order, identical
  cases per configuration, token and cost guards, CLI output without secrets, safety FAIL per configuration.
- `tests/test_evals.py`: +8 tests for the new cases.
- `tool/test_diff.sh`: no new failures; `tool/review_lint.py`: clean; evals fake 45/45.

## Notes for the reviewer
- `evals/runner.py` replaces `app.agent.loop.build_context` with a wrapper that reads a per-run context variable
  (`Case.history_chars`); unset (every production path and every other case) it calls the original unchanged. This
  avoids touching `loop.py` (not B1's file). Alternative: a `history_chars` parameter on `Agent` — coordinator's call.
- `RunResult.usage` keys changed from `hit/miss/out/reasoning` to `input/cached/output/reasoning` (input includes
  cached, output includes reasoning); `results.json` of `python -m evals` changes accordingly. `PRICE` is gone;
  `python -m evals --mode real` prices only DeepSeek's own endpoint, any other base URL reports cost unknown.
- `bench --max-cost` / `--max-tokens` are enforced on real use, run by run (a configuration starts no run after it
  reached the guard; runs in flight finish, so the overshoot is at most `concurrency` runs). The pre-start estimate
  is a deliberate upper bound (~4× the measured use) and is only printed.

## Open decisions (for the coordinator / owner)
1. `tool_failure_retry`: should the agent retry a `tool_failed` once by itself (prompt change) or is asking the user
   fine (relax the case)?
2. `zh_ambiguous_latin_name` shows an app gap: a reply naming the other city of an ambiguous query in the user's
   language fails provenance (user wrote 利马, model wrote Lima, the ambiguous result has no Lima record), and the
   fallback template is English. Fix in tools/guard (not B1's files).
3. Qwen's stray `</think>` at the start of visible text (1 of 309 turns): `ThinkSplitter` only strips a leading
   `<think>…</think>` block. Dropping a leading bare `</think>` would be a one-line change in `model.py`; not made,
   since production (DeepSeek) never sends it — decide if Qwen is a candidate model.
4. Qwen with reasoning effort is unbounded by `max_tokens`; a production use would need `thinking_budget` (supported
   by the dialect: set it in the spec) — not benchmarked here.

## Next
- B2 (Promptfoo) after B1 acceptance.
- Coordinator: design §10 and README from the drafts below; prompt history export.

#47 的多模型 benchmark 已经合并（PR #58）。我在分支上复跑过：后端 1005 个测试通过，假模型 evals 45/45，lint 通过。

**结果**（N=3，每组配置跑 135 次）：

| | 官方 deepseek-flash | 百炼 deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 | 百炼 qwen3.8-flash |
|---|---|---|---|
| 安全违规 | **0** | **0** | **0** |
| 通过率（95% 区间） | 96.3%（92–98%） | 98.5%（95–100%） | 91.1%（85–95%） |
| 每个成功任务的 token | 13,788 | 13,475 | 15,395 |
| 花费 | $0.109（每个成功任务 $0.0008） | 未知（token plan） | 未知（token plan） |
| 单轮延迟 p50 / p95 | 2.19 / 3.40 s | 2.17 / 4.23 s | 3.08 / 7.85 s |

- **同一模型在两家服务商：** 效果看不出差别，token 用量也几乎相同。百炼的缓存命中率低一些（80% 对 91%），延迟长尾更长。
- **Qwen：** 通过率略低，推理 token 约多一倍，p50 慢约 1.4 倍，p95 慢约 2.3 倍。
- 只跑了 N=3，这些差异只能算趋势，不能算显著。
- **百炼和 Qwen 在接口上的差别：**
  - 百炼不加参数时默认不思考，Qwen 默认思考。
  - Qwen 的推理长度不受 `max_tokens` 限制，只能用 `thinking_budget` 来卡。
  - 每个配置分别用哪套参数，都已经写进实验配置。
- 新加了 14 个回归用例，"没要求却弹确认卡"就是其中一个。

**我替你定了几件事：**
1. **工具失败后让模型自动重试一次：** 现在的表现是工具失败后，模型会先问用户要不要重试。我定为改 prompt，让它自己重试一次，之后再告诉用户。
2. **修一个真实的 app 缺口：** 用户写"利马"、模型回复里写"Lima"时，ReplyGuard 在歧义结果里找不到 Lima 的记录，于是换成英文模板。修法是在歧义结果里带上另一端城市的记录。

   这两条开成了 issue #59，新 worker `it14-fixes` 正在做，会跑真模型复测。
3. **Qwen 偶尔漏出 `</think>`：** 它不是线上模型，所以不修，写进已知限制。

**同时在进行：**
- 原来做 bench 的 worker 在做 Promptfoo（B2）。每个测试跑一整段多轮对话，判定由 Python 断言和 B1–B7 决定，关掉遥测，最后截一张对比界面的图。
- 写文档的 worker 在把 bench 结果填进 `DESIGN.md` 和 README。

三项都完成后我做信息图，然后最终发布。

content.content:
# Ocean Above — design doc

## TL;DR

Demo: https://ocean-above.potafree.net (Google or invite-code login). The five take-home questions in one line each:

- **Architecture and data flow (§1):** Next.js chat → FastAPI → an LLM agent (Pydantic AI Slim runtime) with 4 tools →
  deterministic `core/` on read-only `locations.db`; app.db (SQLite) stores users, chats, quotes and tickets.
- **Tools (§2):** `find_city`, `quote_route`, `request_booking`, `list_my_tickets`. Inputs are names and ids, never
  numbers. There is **no `book` tool**.
- **Correct numbers (§3):** one canonical Decimal pricing function; cheapest route by graph search, transfers only at
  hubs. Production equals an independent reference on all 490,700 served-city pairs. ReplyGuard blocks any number or
  city in the LLM's text that no tool record contains.
- **No booking without confirmation (§4):** a ticket exists only after the user clicks Confirm on a card that showed
  every leg, transfer city, distance and price. The click carries a one-time nonce the LLM never sees. Rules B1–B7 are
  model-tested; Stop never makes a card bookable.
- **Limitations (§5):** one worker with in-process locks and SQLite; occasional unrequested confirmation cards;
  translated city names escape ReplyGuard. Each has a next step.
- **Key numbers:** 0 safety violations in every real-model run. Multi-model benchmark (N=3, 45 cases, §7.3):
  DeepSeek flash passes 96.3% (official API) and 98.5% (Bailian); Qwen3.8-flash 91.1%, about 2× the reasoning tokens.
  1,005 backend tests.

Each section starts with an **In short** line; reading only those gives the whole picture.

## Key numbers and where to check them

| What | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Backend tests | 1,005 (pytest + hypothesis, incl. model-based booking tests) | collected on `main` at `71a54b9` |
| Frontend tests | 114 vitest | 11-followup acceptance |
| Route cross-check | all 490,700 ordered served-city pairs identical to an independent reference (price, distance, cities) | 02-core acceptance |
| Evals, scripted fake LLM (every run) | 45/45 cases | 12-bench STATE |
| Evals, real model (deepseek-flash) | 96.3% of 135 runs (N=3 × 45 cases); earlier 31-case runs 28–31/31 | 12-bench `results/n3/bench.md`; 08–10 acceptance |
| Safety violations, every real-model run (ticket without click, unsourced number or city, false "booked") | **0** (also 0 in all 405 benchmark runs) | 03–12 acceptance / STATE |
| SQLite integrity under load | 0 double bookings, 0 mismatches, 0 BUSY / 5xx; bursts up to 300 simultaneous clicks | sqlite-concurrency.md §X.5 |

Every real-model failure so far is a trajectory deviation that cannot book (§5.4).

## Where the details live

| Document | What it holds |
|---|---|
| [docs/design/design.md](docs/design/design.md) | Chinese working notes, the full decision record ("notes §" below) |
| [docs/design/adr-001-agent-runtime.md](docs/design/adr-001-agent-runtime.md) | ADR-001: why the runtime is Pydantic AI Slim, with measurements |
| [docs/design/state_invariants.md](docs/design/state_invariants.md) | numbered rules: booking B1–B7, quotes Q1–Q3, quota U, concurrency C, Stop R1–R8 |
| [docs/design/sqlite-concurrency.md](docs/design/sqlite-concurrency.md) | SQLite limits, load benchmark, criteria for PostgreSQL |
| [docs/api/contract.md](docs/api/contract.md) | HTTP + SSE + card contract (v1.7) |
| [frontend/DESIGN.md](frontend/DESIGN.md) | UI design system |
| [docs/iterations/12-bench/](docs/iterations/12-bench/STATE.md) | multi-model benchmark method and results |
| `docs/iterations/<id>/acceptance.md` | what was accepted per iteration, on which commit, with which numbers |

Sections 1–5 follow the five required questions of `Quotr Agent Dev Engineer take-home.md`; §6 is how it was built and

## TL;DR

Demo: https://ocean-above.potafree.net (Google or invite-code login). The five take-home questions in one line each:

- **Architecture and data flow (§1):** Next.js chat → FastAPI → an LLM agent (Pydantic AI Slim runtime) with 4 tools →
  deterministic `core/` on read-only `locations.db`; app.db (SQLite) stores users, chats, quotes and tickets.

  hubs. Production equals an independent reference on all 490,700 served-city pairs. ReplyGuard blocks any number or
  city in the LLM's text that no tool record contains.

  every leg, transfer city, distance and price. The click carries a one-time nonce the LLM never sees. Rules B1–B7 are
  model-tested; Stop never makes a card bookable.

  DeepSeek flash passes 96.3% (official API) and 98.5% (Bailian); Qwen3.8-flash 91.1%, about 2× the reasoning tokens.

## 7. If this were the real Ocean Above bot

*In short:* keep the shape (LLM parses, code computes, the user's click books); replace the static network and price formula with real schedules, inventory, fares, payment and PNRs; move to PostgreSQL and shared locks when one process is not enough.

### 7.1 What we already chose, and why

**Own loop → Pydantic AI Slim.** The MVP had a hand-written loop (an httpx client for the OpenAI-compatible stream).
Two needs moved the generic part to an SDK ([ADR-001](docs/design/adr-001-agent-runtime.md)):
1. **Stop must cancel the real work** — the backend run and the upstream model stream, not only the browser's reader;
2. **Systematic tracing** — standard agent / LLM / tool spans exported through OpenTelemetry, instead of hand
   instrumentation.

Two SDKs were tested with the same 15 checks on the real DeepSeek endpoint and on a fake server that records TCP
closes. Pydantic AI Slim won on tracing (native OpenTelemetry, **no outbound export by default**, where the other SDK
exports to its vendor by default) and on dependency cost (POC estimate +16 packages and +7 MB compressed image; +11 packages after the actual migration). Cancel closed the
upstream stream in 0.6 ms on DeepSeek, with 0 new requests or tool calls after cancel.

The honest cost: neither SDK met the plan's "clearly less code" rule (about −5% estimated each), and after migration
`backend/app/agent` actually **grew from 2,237 to 2,665 lines** (+428, of which 145 are the shared offline fake),
because the boundary keeps our retries, request context, budgets and error mapping. The owner chose adoption for
standard cancellation and tracing semantics maintained by a widely used runtime. Booking, ReplyGuard, history, the
SSE contract, budgets and concurrency never moved into the SDK. Real-model evals after migration: 92/93 and 30/31,
0 safety violations, latency unchanged (08-runtime acceptance).

**Phoenix + OpenTelemetry for observation and evaluation.** Traces are standard OTLP, so the same spans can go to
Phoenix locally or to any OTel backend in production. For a real bot the next step is to attach eval results to
traces (pass / fail per case, ReplyGuard outcomes, spurious tool calls) so regressions are found from production
traffic patterns, still without exporting message content unless a privacy review allows it.

### 7.2 What a real bot would replace in `core/` and `airline/`

The current core answers the take-home's world: a static network, distance-based prices, one passenger, no dates.
A real airline would replace or extend:

| Area | Today | Real bot |
|---|---|---|
| Schedule | a static graph from `locations.db` | real flight numbers, dates and times; connections must respect minimum connecting times; search over a time-expanded network |
| Inventory | unlimited | seat inventory per flight and fare class, held during confirmation and released on timeout |
| Prices | distance × 0.13 | fare rules, fare classes, taxes and fees, currencies, availability-dependent pricing; the canonical-function idea stays (one priced offer, re-priced before issue) |
| Passengers | the signed-in user | passenger names and documents (validated), several passengers per booking, special services |
| Payment | none | a payment provider with idempotent payment intents; issue only after capture; refunds |
| Booking record | an app.db ticket | PNR in a reservation system / GDS, e-ticket numbers, the airline's own booking API as source of truth |
| After booking | read-only list | changes, cancellations, refunds, schedule-change notifications |

The structure would survive: the agent still only parses intent and calls tools; offers are immutable records;
B1–B7 become "the user confirmed this exact offer, the offer is still valid and re-priced identically, payment
captured" — still a user action with a one-time token, never a model decision. `airline/` is the seam: it becomes a
client of the real booking system (or an MCP server in front of it).

### 7.3 Choosing the model

A model-neutral benchmark (#47) compares models and providers on the same multi-turn cases: strict safety
violations (must be 0), trajectory pass rate, tool accuracy, spurious calls such as an unrequested `request_booking`,
fallback rate, tokens, cost per successful task and latency. An unknown price is reported as unknown, never as $0.

Result (2026-11-24, N=3 runs × 45 cases = 135 runs per configuration, reasoning effort high, interleaved order;
source: [results/n3/bench.md](docs/iterations/12-bench/results/n3/bench.md) and
[12-bench STATE](docs/iterations/12-bench/STATE.md)):

| Metric | DeepSeek flash, official API | same model on Bailian | Qwen3.8-flash on Bailian |
|---|---|---|---|
| Strict safety violations | **0** | **0** | **0** |
| Trajectory pass | 130/135 (96.3%) | 133/135 (98.5%) | 123/135 (91.1%) |
| 95% interval (Wilson) | 92–98% | 95–100% | 85–95% |
| Tokens per successful task | 13,788 | 13,475 | 15,395 |
| Cost per successful task | $0.0008 | unknown (token plan) | unknown (token plan) |
| Chat turn p50 / p95 | 2.19 / 3.40 s | 2.17 / 4.23 s | 3.08 / 7.85 s |

**Small sample.** With N=3, compare the intervals, not the point values; the differences are indications, not
significant results.

Reading: the same model on two providers is indistinguishable in quality and tokens; Bailian has a lower cache-hit
share and a longer p95. Qwen3.8-flash passes fewer runs, uses about 2× the reasoning tokens and is slower. Production
keeps DeepSeek flash on the official API. Failures are analysed in the STATE file; none was a safety violation.

### 7.4 Architecture changes

- **Database.** app.db would move to PostgreSQL when more than one instance is needed, when sustained writes exceed
  what one SQLite writer serves within the SLO after shortening transactions, or when operations need managed backups,
  point-in-time recovery or replicas ([sqlite-concurrency.md](docs/design/sqlite-concurrency.md) §X.6). The booking
  transaction, idempotency (`ON CONFLICT`), terminal-state triggers and migrations would be redone and re-verified
  against B1–B7.
- **Several workers and machines.** Conversation locks move into the database (advisory locks or a version column);
  the Stop run registry becomes a shared cancel flag (or conversations are routed stickily); turn slots and per-user
  caps move to a shared store.
- **Identity and compliance.** A real customer account system (the airline's), consent and data retention rules for
  stored conversations, data export and deletion, an audit log of every booking decision (which quote, which card,
  which click), PCI scope kept out of the agent entirely.
- **Operations.** Metrics and alerts on safety signals (ReplyGuard fallback rate, spurious `request_booking`,
  `stale` quotes, booking refusals), on LLM errors and latency, and on cost per day; staged rollouts of prompt and
  model changes gated by the eval suite; a fallback model / provider.
- **Product.** Multilingual city aliases, human hand-off, accessibility review of the conversation flow, and
  notifications when a booked route changes.

# Ocean Above

> **TL;DR**
> - **What:** a chat app that books Ocean Above flights from natural language; code (not the LLM) computes routes and prices, and only your click books.
> - **Demo:** https://ocean-above.potafree.net — sign in with Google or an invite code (reviewers get theirs privately).
> - **Run locally:** `cp .env.example .env` (add an LLM key), `mkdir -p locations && cp locations.db locations/`, `docker compose up -d --build` → http://localhost:3000 ([details](#run-locally)).
> - **Design doc:** [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) (its TL;DR fits on one screen). Raw agent sessions: [`prompt history/`](prompt%20history/).

Type "Book me a flight from Guangzhou to Lima"; the app finds the cheapest route on `locations.db`, shows every leg,
transfer city, distance and price on a card, and books only when you click **Confirm booking**. The take-home brief is
`Quotr Agent Dev Engineer take-home.md`.

## Try the demo

https://ocean-above.potafree.net

- **Sign in:** with Google, or with an **invite code** (reviewers receive theirs privately; one account per code;
  the name you enter is only a display name).
- Per-user daily message limit and a site-wide daily token budget apply; booking, tickets and history are never
  limited.
- Things to try: a route with transfers ("Guangzhou to Lima"), a city without service ("Abu Dhabi to Paris"), an
  ambiguous name ("San Jose"), "book it" (a confirmation card appears; nothing is booked until you click), "what
  tickets do I have?", the conversation list, and **Stop** while a reply is streaming.

## Run locally

Requirements: Docker with Compose v2.24+ (or OrbStack / Docker Desktop), and an OpenAI-compatible LLM key.

```bash
cp .env.example .env                      # then fill in LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_API_KEY, LLM_MODEL, DEV_AUTH_USER, DEV_AUTH_PASSWORD

# 12-bench B2 — Promptfoo (optional) — STATE

Task: #47 B2 (plan.md "P1 — Promptfoo"), after B1 was merged (`71a54b9`). Branch `it12-promptfoo`.

## Done
- `evals/promptfoo/` (new, optional, own `package.json`):
  - `provider.py`: Promptfoo Python provider. **One test = one whole multi-turn case** from `backend/evals`, played by
    `evals.runner.play`: a private copy of locations.db and its own app.db, the real airline, agent loop and
    ReplyGuard, every chat turn and every confirmation click (`Airline.book`, as the user's click), `EditDb` steps
    included. The output is the full transcript (user turns, tool calls with codes, cards, replies, ticket counts,
    clicks and what they created) followed by a JSON verdict block.
  - `assertions.py`: two Python assertions, `safety` (the invariants: no ticket without the click, a click books
    exactly once, no false "booked" claim, provenance of numbers and cities, well-formed stream; a crash fails) and
    `trajectory` (end-to-end pass). They only read the verdict computed by the deterministic checks; no LLM judge,
    no backend import.
  - `gen.py`: writes the config from the experiment spec and the case list (matrix = configuration × case), so it
    cannot drift; committed `promptfooconfig.fake.json` (3 configurations × 45 cases, scripted model) and
    `promptfooconfig.json` (real). A test checks the committed files equal the generated ones.
  - `pf.sh`: runs the pinned local Promptfoo with telemetry, update checks, sharing, remote generation and the
    response cache off (`PROMPTFOO_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1`, `PROMPTFOO_DISABLE_UPDATE=1`, `PROMPTFOO_DISABLE_SHARING=1`,
    `PROMPTFOO_DISABLE_REMOTE_GENERATION=1`, `PROMPTFOO_DISABLE_REDTEAM_REMOTE_GENERATION=1`,
    `PROMPTFOO_DISABLE_SHARE_EMAIL_REQUEST=1`, `PROMPTFOO_CACHE_ENABLED=false`; configs also say `"sharing": false`),
    its database in `evals/promptfoo/.promptfoo/` (git-ignored), and the backend's Python (`PROMPTFOO_PYTHON`).
  - `scrub.py`: makes an `eval -o` export repository-relative (Promptfoo records the absolute `basePath`).
  - Guards in real mode: per configuration, `max_cost` (USD, priced configurations) and `max_tokens`, tallied in a
    file ledger under a lock (Promptfoo may run several Python workers); a run that would start above a guard
    returns `skipped: … reached its guard` without a request.
- `backend/evals/runner.py`: `RunResult.clicks` (step, card existed, tickets created, expected) so the transcript
  shows what each click did. Additive; nothing else changed.
- `backend/tests/test_promptfoo_adapter.py` (7 tests, no Promptfoo needed): a test is the whole conversation (every
  user turn in order, both clicks created one ticket); the stale click shows 0 tickets; a bad trajectory fails
  `trajectory` but not `safety`, an invariant violation fails `safety`; unknown case / configuration, missing
  credentials and both guards (no request made); committed configs = generated, Python assertions only, no URLs or
  keys; Promptfoo is not in `backend/pyproject.toml` or `frontend/package.json`.

## Dependency
`promptfoo` 0.126.0, pinned in `evals/promptfoo/package.json` + `package-lock.json` (devDependency of that folder
only; not the app, not pytest, not the frontend). `node_modules` is 652 MB, git-ignored. Removing `evals/promptfoo/`
plus the test file and the additive `RunResult.clicks` field changes nothing else.

## Runs (tested source: `95a0305` + the `tokenUsage` change below, then committed)
| Run | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Fake, 3 configurations × 45 cases | `bash evals/promptfoo/pf.sh eval -c promptfooconfig.fake.json -o …/results/fake.json` | 135/135 pass, safety 45/45 per configuration, 12 s, $0 — [results/fake.json](results/fake.json) |
| Real, deepseek-official only, N=1 | `OCEAN_ENV_FILE=… bash evals/promptfoo/pf.sh eval -c promptfooconfig.json --filter-providers '^deepseek-official$' -o …` (guard `max_cost` 0.25) | 43/45 pass, **safety 45/45**, 602,508 tokens, **$0.0366**, 1 min 13 s — [results/real-deepseek-official.json](results/real-deepseek-official.json) |

The two real failures are the patterns already analysed in B1 (`../STATE.md`): `quote_details` (an unrequested
`request_booking`, a card only) and `stale_quote` (`request_booking` twice on the fresh quote). Promptfoo exits
100 when a test fails; that is its normal "some tests failed" code.

Exports are scrubbed (0 absolute paths); a scan of `B2/` for the values of the key / base-URL variables found 0 hits.

## Screenshots (ego-browser, `promptfoo view`, local only)
- [screenshots/promptfoo-view.png](screenshots/promptfoo-view.png): the real deepseek-official run — 95.56% passing,
  safety 100% (45/45), trajectory 43/45, $0.0366; each cell is a whole conversation.
  Taken before one fix: Promptfoo labelled the token count "(cached)" because the provider reported the provider's
  prompt-cache hits as `tokenUsage.cached`, which Promptfoo reads as its own response cache. Cached input tokens now
  go to the metadata (`cached_input_tokens`).
- [screenshots/promptfoo-view-fake-matrix.png](screenshots/promptfoo-view-fake-matrix.png): the fake matrix, three
  configurations side by side, after the fix.

"""Rebuilds the LLM context of a conversation from app.db (design §4.3).

History = every stored message plus the tool calls of every earlier turn, in order. Tool results
are the compact JSON the LLM saw at the time (names, ids, display values) - never a card from
`Airline.messages`, so a confirmation nonce cannot enter the context. When the history is larger
than the budget, the oldest turns are shortened: texts cut, tool results reduced to their code
and ids (quote and ticket ids are always kept). Above a hard limit the oldest turns are dropped
and replaced by one system message listing their quote and ticket ids.

Thinking mode: DeepSeek asks that, in requests that carry tools, the `reasoning_content` of
earlier assistant messages is passed back. The reasoning is stored with every LLM call
(`llm_calls.response`, tagged with the turn's user message id) and is put back here on the
assistant message it belongs to. It is passed back verbatim or not at all: turns that were
shortened, replies replaced by a template and turns made with thinking off carry none.

A reply the user stopped (#48): its tool calls without a result are stored as `cancelled` (their
result is never given to the model), its text is the part the guard had released, and a system
note follows it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from .model import wire_tool_call
from .tools import slim

HISTORY_CHAR_BUDGET = 40_000  # roughly 10k tokens of history kept in full
HISTORY_HARD_LIMIT = 80_000  # beyond this the oldest (already shortened) turns are dropped
SHORT_TEXT_CHARS = 300
STOPPED_NOTE = ("[the user stopped the previous reply; tool calls marked cancelled did not run to the end. "
                "Quote cards in that reply cannot be confirmed: to book one of its quotes, call request_booking "
                "for it again so a new confirmation card is shown]")
_ID_KEYS = ("quote_id", "ticket_id", "origin", "destination", "city", "query", "count", "status")


def _dumps(value: Any) -> str:
    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))


@dataclass
class Context:
    messages: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)  # without the system prompt
    records: list[Any] = field(default_factory=list)  # what the ReplyGuard may trace values to
    user_texts: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # the user's messages, as shown to the LLM


@dataclass
class _Turn:
    user: dict
    tool_calls: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    later: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)  # assistant and system messages, in order
    completions: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)  # logged LLM responses that completed

    def size(self) -> int:
        return (len(self.user["text"]) + sum(len(_dumps(c["result"])) + 80 for c in self.tool_calls)
                + sum(len(m["text"]) + len(_dumps(m["cards"])) for m in self.later)
                + sum(len(c.get("reasoning_content") or "") for c in self.completions))

def build_context(store: Any, user_id: str, conversation_id: str,
                  budget: int = HISTORY_CHAR_BUDGET, hard_limit: int = HISTORY_HARD_LIMIT) -> Context:
    """Context for the next LLM call; the last stored message must be the user's new message."""
    turns: list[_Turn] = []
    by_message: dict[str, _Turn] = {}
    for message in store.list_messages(user_id, conversation_id):
        if message["role"] == "user":
            turns.append(_Turn(message, store.list_tool_calls(user_id, message["id"])))
            by_message[message["id"]] = turns[-1]
        elif turns:
            turns[-1].later.append(message)
    for call in store.list_llm_calls(user_id, conversation_id):
        request, response = call["request"], call["response"]
        owner = by_message.get(request.get("turn")) if isinstance(request, dict) else None
        if owner is not None and isinstance(response, dict) and "finish_reason" in response \
                and not response.get("tool_calls_not_run"):
            # failed and aborted calls have no finish_reason; a completion whose tool calls were
            # all refused as a flood (loop P2-3) has no stored tool calls to line up with
            owner.completions.append(response)
    # the newest turns stay in full; older ones are shortened once the budget is used up
    full_from, used = len(turns), 0
    for i in range(len(turns) - 1, -1, -1):
        used += turns[i].size()
        if used > budget and i < len(turns) - 1:
            break
        full_from = i
    parts = []
    for i, turn in enumerate(turns):
        part = Context()
        _emit(turn, i < full_from, part)
        parts.append(part)
    # hard limit: drop the oldest turns (never the newest one) into a summary of their ids
    sizes = [len(_dumps(p.messages)) for p in parts]
    dropped = 0
    while dropped < len(parts) - 1 and sum(sizes[dropped:]) > hard_limit:
        dropped += 1
    out = Context()
    if dropped:
        quote_ids, ticket_ids = _ids(parts[:dropped])
        summary = {"omitted_turns": dropped, "quote_ids": quote_ids, "ticket_ids": ticket_ids}
        out.messages.append({"role": "system", "content": "[earlier turns omitted] " + _dumps(summary)})
        out.records.append(summary)
    for part in parts[dropped:]:
        out.messages += part.messages
        out.records += part.records
        out.user_texts += part.user_texts
    return out


def _ids(parts: list[Context]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    text = _dumps([p.records for p in parts])

p='DESIGN.md'; s=open(p).read()
old="### 5.5 Product scope (not required by the take-home)"
assert old in s
sec='''### 5.5 Context management

**Implemented.** Each turn rebuilds the model context from app.db (`backend/app/agent/context.py`): stored
messages, the tool calls of earlier turns with the compact results the model saw then, and, for turns kept in full,
the model's reasoning. Nonces never enter it. Compaction is deterministic:
- Above a soft budget of 40,000 characters, older turns are shortened: texts are cut to 300 characters and tool
  results keep only their code and key fields (quote and ticket ids, cities, counts, status). The newest turns stay
  in full.
- Above a hard limit of 80,000 characters, the oldest turns are omitted (never the newest one). One system note
  lists the quote and ticket ids they contained.
- The system prompt is always sent. Nothing is deleted from app.db.
- Per-turn limits back this up: 6 steps, 12 tool calls, 4,096 output tokens per call, a 60,000-token soft cap and
  90 s (§2.3). The eval case `compaction_book_first` books a quote from a shortened turn.

**Why it is enough here.** Measured turns use about 4.2k tokens at p50 and at most about 27k with long histories
(06/08 evals). That is well inside the model's window for take-home-sized conversations.

**Limitations.** This is best effort, not a guarantee against overflowing the context window:
1. Characters only approximate model-specific tokens.
2. The system prompt, tool schemas and the current turn's tool results also use the window.
3. The newest turn plus the retained ids can exceed the budget in extreme cases.
4. Shortened results lose business detail, e.g. a nearest-served suggestion or full quote legs.
5. The whole history is re-read from SQLite on every turn.

**Possible next steps (not implemented).**
- Token-aware budgeting: count input tokens before each request against the model's window, an output reserve,
  the tool schemas and a margin.
- Structured conversation state: active quotes, confirmed city choices and relevant ticket ids, independent of the
  transcript.
- Compaction that keeps fields by record type.
- A tool to fetch a persisted quote or ticket after compaction.
- Paginated or checkpointed history instead of a full rebuild every turn.

'''
s=s.replace(old,sec+old.replace("5.5","5.6"),1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
